# Isotope > Examples > Basic Examples

This example finds the five isotopes with the smallest mass defect, which is a measure of how much mass is lost when nucleons are bound together in a nucleus. It then lists these five isotopes, which include lithium-3, boron-6, protium, beryllium-5, and deuterium. This can be useful for research in nuclear physics and understanding the energy characteristics of various isotopes.

```wl
In[1]:= class = \[FreeformPrompt]["5 smallest isotopes by mass defect"]

Out[1]= EntityClass["Isotope", {EntityProperty["Isotope", "MassDefect"] -> TakeSmallest[5]}]

In[2]:= EntityList[class]

Out[2]= {Entity["Isotope", "Lithium3"], Entity["Isotope", "Boron6"], Entity["Isotope", "Hydrogen1"], Entity["Isotope", "Beryllium5"], Entity["Isotope", "Hydrogen2"]}
```

</result>

Use the following information to write Wolfram Language code that involves `Entity`, `EntityClass`, `EntityProperty`, etc. objects.

# Retrieving values for named entities or entity classes

Retrieve a value for a property of a specific entity, entities, or named entity class(es):

```wl
EntityValue[\[FreeformPrompt]["entity or entity class name(s)", "entity type"], "property canonical name"]
```

Include `"Association"` in the third argument of `EntityValue` when requesting more than one entity, entity group and/or property; this returns an association with `Entity` and/or `EntityProperty` objects as keys:

```wl
EntityValue[\[FreeformPrompt]["entity or entity group name(s)", "entity type"], {"property canonical name", ...}, "Association"]
```

The full set of valid values for the third argument of `EntityValue` are:

| Value | Description |
| ----- | --- |
| "EntityAssociation" | an association of entities and entity-property values |
| "PropertyAssociation" | an association of properties and entity-property values |
| "EntityPropertyAssociation" | an association in which the specified entities are keys, and values are a nested association of properties and entity-property values |
| "PropertyEntityAssociation" | an association in which the specified properties are keys, and values are a nested association of entities and entity-property values |
| "Dataset" | a dataset in which the specified entities are keys, and values are an association of property names and entity-property values |
| "Association" | a nested association with entity keys on the first level and property keys on the second level |
| "NonMissingPropertyAssociation" | an association of properties and entity-property values with the missing values dropped |
| "NonMissingEntityAssociation" | an association of entities and entity-property values with the missing values dropped |

# Filtering entities by property values

If an `EntityProperty` can be used to perform an `EntityClass` lookup, use this syntax with specified patterns for `selector`:

```wl
EntityList[EntityClass["entity type",
	{
		EntityProperty["entity type", "property canonical name", {"qualifier name" -> "value name"}] -> selector,
		EntityProperty["entity type", "property canonical name", {"qualifier name" -> "value name"}] -> selector,
		...
	}
]]
```

Note that several selectors may be combined in a single `EntityClass` expression. This is usually the most efficient method of filtering entities.

# Converting natural language to Wolfram Language expressions

Unless exceptions are noted in the instructions for a specific `EntityProperty`, NEVER write `Entity[type, name]` expressions yourself; ALWAYS use \[FreeformPrompt] syntax, as in the examples shown here, to convert natural language names into valid Wolfram expressions.

i.e. NEVER write `Entity["Building", "EmpireStateBuilding"]` in code; ALWAYS write `\[FreeformPrompt]["Empire State Building"]`.

Additional examples:

```wl
\[FreeformPrompt]["Pennsylvania", Entity]
\[FreeformPrompt]["lanthanide elements", EntityClass]
\[FreeformPrompt]["30 m", Quantity]
\[FreeformPrompt]["January 20, 1987", DateObject]
```

In code results, `Missing["UnknownEntity", ...]` indicates that you used an invalid entity standard name. Try again using \[FreeformPrompt] syntax.

# Isotope > Examples > Basic Examples

This example finds the isotope with the smallest mass excess among all isotopes and identifies it as tin-118. The result provides insight into nuclear properties, as mass excess relates to the binding energy and stability of a nucleus.

```wl
In[1]:= class = \[FreeformPrompt]["isotope with the smallest mass excess"]

Out[1]= EntityClass["Isotope", {EntityProperty["Isotope", "MassExcess"] -> TakeSmallest[1]}]

In[2]:= EntityList[class]

Out[2]= {Entity["Isotope", "Tin118"]}
```

</result>

# EntityProperty > Isotope > AtomicMass

Entity type: `"Isotope"` (Variants of a given chemical element that differ in neutron number.)
Property full name: `EntityProperty["Isotope", "AtomicMass"]`
Property canonical name: `"AtomicMass"`
Property common name: `"atomic mass"`
Sample property value: `Quantity[235.043928117`7.99166222283511, "AtomicMassUnit"]`
Supports `EntityClass` lookups: `True`

Sample `selector` expressions to use with `EntityClass` lookups:
```wl
{EntityProperty["Isotope", "AtomicMass", {qualifier -> value}] -> TakeLargest[integer]}
{EntityProperty["Isotope", "AtomicMass", {qualifier -> value}] -> Interval[{\[FreeformPrompt]["minimum quantity", Quantity], \[FreeformPrompt]["maximum quantity", Quantity]}]}
{EntityProperty["Isotope", "AtomicMass", {qualifier -> value}] -> EqualTo[\[FreeformPrompt]["quantity", Quantity]]}
{EntityProperty["Isotope", "AtomicMass", {qualifier -> value}] -> GreaterThan[\[FreeformPrompt]["quantity", Quantity]]}
```

Property qualifiers:
	Sample qualifier usage: 
	`EntityProperty["Isotope", "AtomicMass", {"Uncertainty" -> "Around"}]`

	Valid qualifiers:
		Qualifier: `"Uncertainty"`
		  Values: 
		    `"Around"` (Around)
		    `"Interval"` (Interval)
		    `"Precision"` (Precision)
		    `"Automatic"` (Automatic)

(Up to 25 values shown per qualifier. If a suitable value isn't shown, do not invent one; evaluate `EntityProperty["Isotope", "AtomicMass"]["QualifierValues"]` for full list.)

</result>

# Isotope > Examples > Basic Examples

Define the entity class for stable isotopes and list all isotopes belonging to this class, returning a collection of isotopes that do not undergo radioactive decay.

In[1]:= class = \[FreeformPrompt]["stable isotopes"]

Out[1]= EntityClass["Isotope", "Stable"]

In[2]:= EntityList[class]

Out[2]= {Entity["Isotope", "Hydrogen1"], Entity["Isotope", "Hydrogen2"], Entity["Isotope", "Helium3"], Entity["Isotope", "Helium4"], Entity["Isotope", "Lithium6"], Entity["Isotope", "Lithium7"], Entity["Isotope", "Beryllium9"], Entity["Isotope", "Boron10"] ... ["Isotope", "Mercury202"], Entity["Isotope", "Mercury204"], Entity["Isotope", "Thallium203"], Entity["Isotope", "Thallium205"], Entity["Isotope", "Lead204"], Entity["Isotope", "Lead206"], Entity["Isotope", "Lead207"], Entity["Isotope", "Lead208"]}

</result>

# Isotope > Examples > Entity Properties

Retrieve the brief symbolic notation for uranium-235, displaying the atomic symbol "U" with the mass number 235 as a superscript.

```wl
In[1]:= \[FreeformPrompt]["uranium-235 brief symbol"]

Out[1]= Row[{Superscript["", 235], "U"}]
```

</result>

# Isotope > Examples > Entity Properties

Retrieve the critical mass of uranium-235, which is the minimum amount of the isotope needed to sustain a nuclear chain reaction.

```wl
In[1]:= \[FreeformPrompt]["uranium-235 critical mass"]

Out[1]= Quantity[52.`2., "Kilograms"]
```

</result>

# Isotope > Examples > Basic Examples

This example identifies and lists the five isotopes with the lowest critical mass values. Critical mass is the minimum amount of fissile material needed to sustain a nuclear chain reaction. The isotopes returned include californium-251, californium-249, curium-247, neptunium-236, and curium-243.

```wl
In[1]:= class = \[FreeformPrompt]["5 smallest isotopes by critical mass"]

Out[1]= EntityClass["Isotope", {EntityProperty["Isotope", "CriticalMass"] -> TakeSmallest[5]}]

In[2]:= EntityList[class]

Out[2]= {Entity["Isotope", "Californium251"], Entity["Isotope", "Californium249"], Entity["Isotope", "Curium247"], Entity["Isotope", "Neptunium236"], Entity["Isotope", "Curium243"]}
```

</result>
